title: An accelerated body at constant speed
promptMarkdown: A particle follows $\mathbf x(t)=(R\cos\omega t,R\sin\omega t,0)$ with $R\omega=3c/5$. Compute $U$ and $A$, verify $U\cdot U=-c^2$ and $U\cdot A=0$, and find the proper-acceleration magnitude in terms of $R$. Explain why a spacelike four-acceleration does not mean a massive particle travels faster than light.
hintLadder: The Lorentz factor is constant, but the velocity vector is not.
Convert every time derivative using $d/d\tau=\gamma d/dt$.
Use $\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf a=0$ for circular motion.
